description: Hi, we're Interstellar V ! Just like our name means between the stars , we connect our unique skills and backgrounds to take on the NASA Space Challenge. Our main goal is to transform complex NASA data into something fun and easy for the younger generation to understand, while also gaining valuable experience together.
summary: Blast Off! is an interactive space survival adventure for children ages 7-12, built for the Build A Junior Astronaut Mission Training challenge, where YOU become a NASA astronaut cadet running outposts on the Moon and Mars. Space STEM content often oversimplifies real mission trade-offs for young learners, yet Haeusler and Donovan (2017) showed that primary school children can grasp abstract scientific concepts through appropriate learning approaches. So Blast Off! makes them playable: complete missions, collect research data and balance oxygen, food, water, solar power and radiation protection. No choice is free. Saving power today may cost oxygen tomorrow, so every decision has consequences. Successful missions unlock better tools, while mistakes bring new challenges, letting children learn from failure without feeling punished. Varied mission events keep every playthrough fresh, and a leaderboard rewards brave decisions with friendly competition. Every mission is powered by real NASA science, including the LCROSS discovery of lunar water ice, the ISS’s 98% water recovery milestone and the Ingenuity helicopter’s struggle to fly in Mars’ thin atmosphere, with sources credited in-game and terms explained in plain language. Through quizzes, resource management and decision-making, Blast Off! shows children how their choices decide whether a mission fails or succeeds, sparking critical thinking, curiosity and a love for STEM.
details:
Gameplay Feature

In Blast Off!, children blast into space as NASA astronaut cadets, ready to survive on the Moon and Mars! Players begin on the mission screen, where they choose a destination between Mars or Moon. The players will be guided by Dr Farah a senior astronaut where she will help to introduce a real challenge astronauts face, such as limited oxygen, scarce water, power shortages or dangerous radiation.

Next, players manage their outpost by balancing oxygen, food, water, solar power and radiation protection. Every choice has a cost: saving power today may cost oxygen tomorrow. Smart decisions unlock better tools and easier data collection, while mistakes bring new challenges that teach players to try again.

To wrap up the adventure, players complete quizzes based on what they’ve learned, climb the leaderboard and see whether their outpost survived the mission!

Goals

The main goal of Blast Off! is to make learning about space survival engaging, interactive and educational for children. The game encourages curiosity about science and space while building an understanding of how real astronaut decisions, from managing oxygen, food, water, power and radiation protection, determine whether a mission succeeds. By combining storytelling, hands-on exploration and simple scientific explanations grounded in real NASA data, it aims to inspire young learners to see that every brave decision can lead to a big discovery!


Problem Solving Skills

Players learn by exploring cause and effect, understanding how decision in running lunar and mars outpost impact different occupations and the environment. Each challenge encourages critical thinking and scientific reasoning, showing how professionals adapt to space weather events. By following players and Dr Farah, it helps to connect fun storytelling with real science, discovering how running Mars and Lunar Outpost can both challenge and inspire life on Earth.


Key Benefits & Impacts

  • Inspires the next generation: Turns space survival into an adventure that builds children’s curiosity about space exploration and STEM, preparing them for future careers.
  • Supports educators: Gives teachers a ready-to-use classroom tool that teaches STEM concepts and real NASA data through play, in plain language for ages 7-12.
  • Supports NASA planners: Shows that no choice is free, so players see how balancing oxygen, food, water, power and radiation protection decides whether a long-duration lunar or Martian mission succeeds or fails.
  • Makes NASA data accessible: Offers visual, code-free access to NASA data on lunar and Martian outpost missions, with sources credited in-game so the science stays traceable.

Tools & Technologies

  • Figma: Used for UI/UX wireframing, interface design, asset creation and interactive prototyping, so the mission screens and outpost dashboard were tested before any code was written.
  • React: Powers the core UI components and manages game state, tracking resources, mission progress, quizzes and the leaderboard.
  • Three.js & React Three Fiber (R3F): Three.js is the WebGL engine that renders the 3D Moon and Mars outposts, and R3F wraps it in React so interactive 3D scenes, models and environments stay easy to build and update.
  • Web Audio API: Adds sound effects and background music to make the astronaut experience more immersive.
  • Vercel: Hosts the game in the cloud with CI/CD deployment and global edge delivery, so children can play instantly in a browser with no download or account

Creative Elements

  • Story-driven learning: A compelling storyline turns NASA data into real astronaut risks, so children don’t just read facts but live through the dangers of survival on the Moon and Mars, from oxygen shortages to radiation events.
  • Visual data exploration: A kid-friendly interface turns complex NASA data about lunar and Martian outposts into visual exploration, letting players see resources, risks and consequences at a glance instead of reading tables or code.

Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)

We used AI tools to speed up development, design, and content creation.

Google Gemini/Claude: For generating UX copy, synergy logic, and content drafts (all reviewed and edited).

We tested AI tools like Magnific for visuals, but primarily used free stock images. No NASA logos or branding were used in AI outputs.

AI helped accelerate the process, but the research, logic, and direction were fully team-led.
